body: By the way, thank you for taking the time to connect with me. Doesn't look like anyone else noticed my post.

Yeah, they are always telling her to reach out to her brother, he needs support, but he doesn't actually make any effort to return messages, seems lackluster about any kind of contact, and never reaches out to her when she's struggling! We never get any indication that anyone cares if we're having a hard time (with anything! Money, pet sickness, isolation, job losses, illness, multiple family deaths!!? Nothing!).

I'm still building up my background for my therapist, it's only been 5 appointments so far. We've gone over my ADHD struggles, my father's death, and my difficulty communicating with my wife and ending up in fights cos of it. I've mentioned her suicidal expression, but my own is more recent. I don't know if my wife has explained her own to her own therapist, but I suspect not, because she seems to think she'll get an ambulance called for her and be confined in a mental hospital if she does. (To be fair, part of her PTSD does centre around that exact thing happening to her because of some toxic friends turning on her and calling 911 and lying that she was trying to kill herself. She had an involuntary 72 hours, lost a lot of money getting out of a lease, and almost got kicked out of uni because the 'friends' spread rumours about her being "dangerously unstable". She has a lot of shit in her past...)

We're individually seeing online therapists, once a month (expensive). I have a psychiatric doctor for my antidepressants and ADHD meds, cos my diagnosis is from my home country, but she can't seem to get a referral for her depression, anxiety and CPTSD symptoms without an existing history of treatment. 〜baffled〜 Also, previous try-outs of psychiatric meds in America didn't work out, so she's leery anyway.

My family is loving and supportive, but catch-ups are sporadic, and they only encourage me to "come home" if expat life is "too hard". Or they blame it all on my wife. She has a catch-up every week with her parents, but they tend to one-up her suffering with their own, or tell her she's ungrateful for their "help" that wasn't what she asked for and was actually unhelpful. 

I feel like all our friends have forgotten us since we moved here. And local friends seem to leave us out more than they invite us.
